extracted.intended_audience: naturalists, geographers, physicists, and educated readers interested in the physical description (cosmography) of the universe
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for composing a systematic 'physical description of the universe' (physical cosmography), including how to set its limits, method of exposition, relation to allied sciences, and the style and organization suitable for conveying unified, high-level views of terrestrial and sidereal phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use generalization judiciously
rubrics_metrics.description: Favor the tendency to generalization to make physical knowledge widely accessible, but avoid its abuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generalization can make scientific knowledge 'the common property of all classes of society' provided one deviates from the 'imperfect compilations' of popular knowledge; do not over-generalize to the point of distortion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat scientific subjects in dignified, animated language
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific subjects should be presented 'in language at once dignified, grave, and animated.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for style that is readable for those who have been strangers to intimate communion with nature; language should invigorate the mind and awaken dormant perceptive faculties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show practical and industrial relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate how mechanics, chemistry, and other sciences can be made conducive to national prosperity and industrial progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argue that sound propagation of scientific knowledge and its application to arts and industry avert national decline; use historical and practical examples where theoretical work later produced important applications (e.g., Galvani/voltaic discoveries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid arbitrary hierarchies among scientific branches
rubrics_metrics.description: Give equal appreciation to all branches of mathematical, physical, and natural sciences rather than labeling some as less important or 'purely theoretical.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that apparently isolated phenomena may conceal germs of great discoveries; do not stigmatize branches whose utility may later become evident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek unity and unifying principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursue an 'inward' object: the ennoblement of the intellect by striving after knowledge of laws and principles of unity that pervade the vital forces of the universe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concentrate ideas in one common focus to perceive organisms and forces as a single living active whole; emphasize connecting links and simultaneous action of forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not confound cosmography with encyclopedic compilation
rubrics_metrics.description: The science of the Cosmos is not a mere aggregation of results from special branches; partial facts must be considered only in relation to the whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use partial results as materials for a vast edifice that shows connecting links; avoid simply compiling floras, lists, or isolated descriptions without synthesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt a systematic mode of treatment from a high point of view
rubrics_metrics.description: From a higher point of view, the subject requires a more systematic treatment in language that is animated and picturesque.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher-level synthesis demands disciplined organization and style that can present broad relations clearly and vividly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Let language shape and animate thought
rubrics_metrics.description: Language and thought react mutually; a flexible, rich native language enhances exposition and stimulates thinking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use lucid exposition rooted in the native tongue's resources; draw on expressive diction to interpret complex natural phenomena and to animate intellectual presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precisely define the limits of the science
rubrics_metrics.description: Circumscribe the 'physical description of the universe' as a distinct science and distinguish it from analogous or auxiliary studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly set out the precise limits, enumerate encompassed phenomena, discuss the influence of the external world on imagination, and review historical development of the idea of the Cosmos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat terrestrial and sidereal portions appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize the twofold form of cosmography (the earth and the regions of space) and treat each according to its proper methods and certainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appreciate that sidereal phenomena are governed by dynamical laws (laws of motion) and often admit greater mathematical certainty than terrestrial phenomena, which require physics, chemistry, and morphology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin with the celestial (sidereal) description
rubrics_metrics.description: The physical history of the world should begin with the description of the heavenly bodies and a 'geographical sketch of the universe.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not subordinate the sidereal portion to the terrestrial; the sun with its satellites is but one of innumerable stars, and the sidereal map provides essential context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrict physical geography to general, comparative results
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical geography (terrestrial portion) should depict broad outlines—distribution of magnetism, configuration of continents, mountain-chain character, mean heights, river behavior—without entering into specialized enumerations or into laws proper to other sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid treating physical geography as an inventory (e.g., exhaustive lists of peaks, active volcanoes, river tributaries); focus on mutual connections and relations to climatic zones and planetary constitution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use induction and combine isolated observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject isolated observations to the process of thought and combine and compare them to discover relations, numerical laws, and general patterns (e.g., 'law of substitution').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Move beyond catalogues and systems of nature by induction to comprehend proportions of natural families, latitudinal positions of zones, and constancy amid apparent change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize geographic (zonal) relations over pure taxonomic systems for distributional studies
rubrics_metrics.description: In the physical description of vegetation and fauna, consider 'zones of habitation' and 'isothermal bands' rather than only principles of gradation in internal organism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat floras and faunas by their climatic and elevational distribution and the 'law of substitution' whereby species absent in one region are replaced by related species in neighboring zones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge the peculiar character of physical cosmography
rubrics_metrics.description: While cosmography requires general physics and descriptive natural history, it has a peculiar character arising from contemplating all created things as a linked whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use auxiliary sciences as tools, but retain the distinctive aim of showing relations among phenomena across scales and domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat molecular/chemical considerations where relevant but avoid conflating with dynamical celestial mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that terrestrial phenomena involve 'chemical affinity' and molecular actions (modified by electricity, heat, condensation), whereas sidereal mechanics are dominated by gravitation and laws of motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address specific material properties in Earth-focused sections, but understand celestial descriptions may not require such considerations except where meteorites/aerolites inform material composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer appropriate nomenclature and avoid excessive classification splitting
rubrics_metrics.description: Be cautious about imposing inappropriate Greek nomenclature or over-multiplying binary divisions and groups when classifying branches of knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose terms and classificatory schemes that are expressive and broadly understood rather than inventing misleading or excessively technical labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use examples and historical cases to justify methodological choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Support methodological assertions by historical and empirical examples that show how isolated observations led to major discoveries or how different emphases shaped disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite cases like Galvani/voltaic discoveries, Huygens/Arago on polarization, and the development of astronomy and geography to illustrate why certain approaches (e.g., valuing pure theory) are justified.
